title: The determinant of a square matrix (Leibniz formula)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$ an integer and $M=(M_{ik})_{1\le i,k\le m}$ an $m\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. Let $S_m$ be the group of permutations of $\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $\operatorname{sgn}:S_m\to\{\pm1\}$ the sign, the group homomorphism with $\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)=-1$ for every transposition $\tau$. The determinant of $M$ is $$\det M=\sum_{\sigma\in S_m}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{k=1}^{m}M_{\sigma(k),k}\in R.$$ For $m=0$, $S_0$ has one element and the product is empty, so $\det M=1$.
